lawyer: Md Enamul Hoque, Advocate — For the Petitioner.
parties:
Abu Taleb ------ Petitioner
Vs. 
State ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
3. During trial the learned Special Tribunal framed charge against the 5 accused persons including petitioner under section 4(b) of the Explosive Substance Act and since all of them absconded after going on bail the trial proceeded under section 339B(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. During trial prosecution examined 7 PWs out of 11 PWs as mentioned in the charge sheet. The witnesses examined were not cross-examined by the accused persons since they were absconding and that the accused persons including the petitioner could not be examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. After close of the prosecution the learned Special Tribunal in consideration of the evidence on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case found all the accused persons guilty for the offence charged under section 4(b) of the Explosive Substance Act and each of them were sentenced to suffer RI for 3 years. 

 5. Mr. Enamul Hoque, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, read over the FIR, charge sheet, seizure list evidence on record with reference to the impugned judgment and order of conviction. He thereafter submits that the impugned judgment is bad in law and the learned Special Tribunal committed error of law causing error in decision occasioning failure of justice. Mr. Enamul Hoque, the learned Advocate then submits that the learned Special Tribunal did not consider that the alleged recovery/seizure was not made as per provision of section 103 of the CrPC. Mr. Enamul Hoque, the learned Advocate, further submits that the learned Special Tribunal did not consider that none of seizure list witnesses have been examined and in absence of any private witness of the alleged occurrence as well as recovery of the same has not been proved. Mr. Huque, lastly, submits that the learned Special Tribunal failed to consider that the incriminating article ie bomb has not been produced in court and, as such, the alleged recovery has ended in fiasco. Accordingly the impugned judgment and order of conviction for alleged unauthorized possession of the bomb from the control and possession of the accused petitioner is not only bad in law but also illegal. Accordingly, he submits that the impugned judgment and order of conviction is liable to be quashed. 

 7. We have personally read over the FIR, charge sheet, seizure list and evidence on record with reference to the impugned judgment. This case is under section 4(b) of the Explosive Substance Act started on the allegation of recovery of a bomb under control/ possession of the accused petitioner and others. It appears that the prosecution has examined 7 PWs out of 11 as mentioned in the charge sheet. 

 9. PW 2, another police constable, corroborated the PW 1 on all material points. PW 3, S I of Police, claimed that he was on duty at Lalbag PS as S I on 21-5-93 and he was appointed investigation officer of this case by the OC, He claimed that he visited the place of occurrence prepared sketch map of the place of occurrence with separate index which he proved as Ext, 1 and 2 series respectively. He examined the witnesses and recorded their statement under section 161 CrPC, examined the seizure list as well as the alamats of the case and after completion of investigation submitted a charge sheet against the accused persons under section 4(b) of the Explosive Substance Act since prima facie case was made out against them. He further proved the FIR Ext. 3 and signature of the SI Belayet who filled up the same Ext. 3/3. PW 4, Anupam Chakma, SI of Police said that on 21-5-93 he was on duty at Lalbag PS and on that date at 8-00 AM he along with his patrol party was engaged on patrol duty and during the period at about 12-45 hours they reached in front of a shop at 7, Hazaribag Road which is a mutton shop of one Sona Mia and found 7/8 persons talking with each other. He then said that he challenged them when 2/3 fled away therefrom and they apprehended 5 out of them. He mentioned the names of the youths as Abu Taleb, Kamal, Monier Hossain, Omar Farook and Akhter Hossain, He then said that he searched the shop of Sona Mia in presence of local men and a bomb underneath the date leaf mat was recovered which he seized by preparing a seizure list wherein the witnesses signed their names. He further said that he forwarded the accused persons to Lalbagh PS along with seizure list and the article seized. He proved the written ejahar Ext.4 and his signature thereto Ext. 4/2. He also proved the seizure list and his signature thereto Ext.5-5/1 respectively. PW 5 a police Havilder and PW 6 a police Naik corroborated the PWs 1-4 on all material points. PW 7 a constable was tendered by the prosecution. This is all about the evidence on record. 

 11. It also appears from the record that no seizure list witness have been examined in this case nor the prosecution has come with a reasonable explanation for their absence. So it is presumed that had the seizure list witnesses been examined they would not have supported the prosecution case. In this case prosecution is found to have examined 7 witnesses who are none but police personnel and that those police men are directly under control and command of the police officer who lodged the suo motu FIR in this case. So, in such circumstances evidence of these PWs should be swallowed with a grain of salt. Further, it appears the provision of section 103 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was not complied with. Since the search and recovery was not conducted in presence of independent witness, the prosecution case does not find leg to stand upon. The absence of seizure list witness together with absence of incriminating article allegedly recovered from the control/ possession of the accused petitioner and others has made the whole prosecution case unworthy to believe and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction cannot sustain.
